owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to main.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to main as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.
A receipt never overclaims: ran:false is reported as not run, never as pass (ZR-11).
The verifier never controls its own trust boundary: contract, evidence and gate records change only through the owner deploy key.
Heuristic checks are one layer, never a boundary; say so in every receipt and page.
No reliability or enterprise claim without a gated task behind it (TB-08).
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | missing.

tasks.title: generate, load, kid, key files mode 0600
tasks.description: New repository mgillr/agentkey: package.json (name agentkey, type module, engines node>=22, zero dependencies), src/index.mjs exporting generate(role), load(role), kid(publicKey). tasks.title: DSSE sign/verify and in-toto Statement builder
tasks.description: signDSSE(payloadType, payload, key) builds a DSSE envelope: PAE("DSSEv1", payloadType, payload) per the DSSE spec, Ed25519 signature, signatures[0].keyid = kid. verifyDSSE(envelope, keys) returns {verified:[kid...], unknown:[kid...], failed:[kid...]}; a signature that fails for a KNOWN key makes the whole result failed:true (never silently ignored). statement(subjects, predicateType, predicate) returns an in-toto Statement v1 ({"_type":"https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1", subject, predicateType, predicate}). Publish @optitransfer/agentkey@0.1.0-next.0 under dist-tag next with --access public from the maintainer machine, without provenance: npm generates it only inside a CI runner, and GitHub Actions on this account is locked by billing, so the release workflow of AK-06 carries it. Test vectors: the DSSE repository protocol test vectors (vendored under test/vectors/ with their licence), plus an interop test that an envelope signed here verifies with the sigstore npm package verifier in a devDependency-only test.

criteria.statement: DSSE PAE vectors pass; tampered payload fails; unknown keyid reported as unknown; failed known key reported as failed

tasks.title: Binding to the human SSH signing key via ssh-keygen -Y
tasks.description: bind(role, sshKeyPath, principal) runs `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n agentkey -f <sshKey>` over the agent public key and stores <role>.pub.sshsig plus <role>.pub.principal (the e-mail or identity the allowed_signers line names) beside it. verifyBinding(pub, allowedSignersPath, principal) runs `ssh-keygen -Y verify -n agentkey -I <principal> -f <allowedSigners>`. Requires OpenSSH 8.0+; documented. Result vocabulary: bound (verified), unbound (no signature file), invalid (signature present but fails). CLI: agentkey bind <role> --principal <id> [--ssh-key <path>]. ssh-keygen is invoked, never reimplemented. The test generates a throwaway ed25519 SSH key.

criteria.statement: a bound key verifies against an allowed_signers file; an unbound key reports unbound, not invalid; a tampered sshsig reports invalid

tasks.title: Agent identity: honest model, agent-mediated signing, rotation
tasks.description: README and docs state the identity model exactly: a role key identifies the user's role-specific key on that machine, not a unique agent process; every process of that user can read it; isolation options are listed with what each gives. Implemented: AGENTKEY_SIGNER=ssh-agent, where the role key is loaded into ssh-agent with per-use confirmation (`ssh-add -c`) so a signature needs a human confirmation and the private key never sits readable on disk; AGENTKEY_SIGNER=file remains the default and the receipt records `signer: file|ssh-agent|keyless`. Documented option: one OS user per agent with its own AGENTKEY_HOME, and hardware-backed keys via ssh-agent with an `ed25519-sk` token (signatures then verify through ssh-keygen -Y, recorded as signer: sk). Rotation: `agentkey rotate <role>` creates a new key, signs a rotation statement with the old key (old kid, new kid, date) stored in rotations/, sets not_after on the old key; verifiers that know the old kid accept the new one through the chain; hivevault keys trust imports rotation statements with `keys rotate`. Revocation and not_after as in AK-03.

criteria.statement: ssh-agent signer signs through the agent with a confirmation hook and the receipt records signer: ssh-agent; file signer records signer: file
rotate produces a chained statement; a verifier with the old kid accepts the new kid; the old key expires
README states the identity model in the words of the review
